cursed in one breath, flattered in the next. Dare to say, 浮士德, you've never known me.

@@U04557@@
I've spent my life chasing through the world, grabbing at will by the hair all I longed for; what didn’t please, I let go its way, what eluded me, I let escape. My life was desire and satisfaction, and then again desire— and with power and might in my grip I stormed through life; great and mighty at first, but now more wisely, now more prudently. I know this world well, and I know, too, that the view into the world beyond is blocked; and only a fool turns his sheep’s eyes heavenward, imagining men like himself above the clouds! Why go floating off into eternity? Let him stand on firm earth, let him look around him: earth has much to offer the man of worth. What his mind can grasp, that can be his. When he walks, let him walk with his feet on the ground. And if spirits haunt him, ignore them, keep walking, walking, expecting in his path both pain and pleasure, never once in all his earthly progress to know satisfaction.

@@U04559@@

一口气骂了一句，下一秒就受宠若惊。敢说，浮士德，你从来不认识我。

@@U04557@@
我一生都在追寻世界，随意抓住我所渴望的头发；那些令我不高兴的，我就让它顺其自然；那些让我厌烦的，我就让其逃脱。我的生活就是欲望和满足，然后又是欲望——我握着力量和威力，冲过生活；起初伟大而强大，但现在更加明智，现在更加谨慎。我很了解这个世界，也知道外面世界的视野是受阻的；只有傻瓜才会把他的羊的眼睛转向天堂，想象像他一样的人在云端！为什么要飘向永恒？让他站在坚实的大地上，让他环顾四周：大地可以为有价值的人提供很多东西。他的头脑能抓住什么，那就是他的。当他走路时，让他双脚着地。如果灵魂困扰着他，忽略它们，继续走啊走，在他的道路上期待着痛苦和快乐，在他的尘世进步中永远不会有满足感。
